record.paper_title: What Regulates Galaxy Evolution? Open Questions in our Understanding of Galaxy Formation and Evolution.
record.context_brief: Star formation and assembly histories of low-mass galaxies
record.original_question: What are the star formation and assembly histories of galaxies with stellar masses below 10^9 solar masses, including gas-poor dwarf spheroidal galaxies concentrated around more massive galaxies and dwarf irregular galaxies with gas fractions ranging from nearly zero to one that tend to be more isolated?

evidence.quote: Question 2 - What is the star formation and assembly history of galaxies with mass below 10^9 M⊙?

Galaxies with stellar mass below 10^9 M⊙ exhibit a variety of physical properties, from dwarf spheroidals (dSph) that are gas poor and tend to be concentrated around more massive galaxies, to dwarf irregulars (dIrr) whose gas fraction can vary from zero to one, and tend to be more isolated than dSphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the population of galaxies whose stellar mass M_* satisfies M_* < 10^9 M_sun, where M_sun denotes the mass of the Sun. This population spans a wide range of physical properties, including:

(a) dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSph), which are gas-poor and tend to be spatially concentrated around more massive host galaxies; and

(b) dwarf irregular galaxies (dIrr), whose gas fraction f_gas = M_gas / (M_gas + M_*) can vary essentially from 0 to 1 and which tend to be found in more isolated environments than dSphs.

For galaxies in this low-mass regime, determine:

1. Their star formation history, i.e. the function SFR(t) giving the star formation rate as a function of cosmic time t, from formation to the present epoch, including its dependence on stellar mass, gas fraction, and environment.

2. Their assembly history, i.e. how their present-day stellar (and dark matter) mass was assembled over cosmic time through in-situ star formation versus mergers/accretion, again as a function of M_*, gas content, and environment (isolated vs. satellite).

In particular, account for the differences between gas-poor satellite dSphs and gas-rich isolated dIrrs, and identify the physical mechanisms (e.g. reionization, supernova feedback, ram-pressure stripping, tidal interactions) that shape these histories across the M_* < 10^9 M_sun regime.
artifact.status_search_result: The star formation and assembly histories of galaxies below 10^9 M_sun remain an active area of research with many unresolved questions. Recent observational programs (e.g. resolved stellar population studies of Local Group dwarfs, JWST observations of high-redshift dwarfs) and simulations (FIRE, EDGE, etc.) have provided partial constraints, especially for Local Group dSphs, but a comprehensive understanding across the full dwarf-galaxy regime — particularly for isolated dIrrs and at higher redshifts — is still lacking. The problem is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Local Group dwarf galaxies star formation histories review
status_evidence.snippet: Resolved stellar population studies have constrained SFHs of Local Group dwarfs, but uncertainties remain regarding environmental dependence and the role of reionization.
status_evidence.claim: Star formation histories of low-mass galaxies are partially constrained but remain an open research area.

status_evidence.title: JWST observations of high-redshift dwarf galaxies
status_evidence.snippet: JWST is beginning to reveal the assembly of low-mass galaxies at z>6, but linking these to local dwarfs remains an outstanding challenge.
status_evidence.claim: Assembly histories of low-mass galaxies remain incompletely understood.
